title: [Bug] Large scale PD Disagression bug : cascading failure in Decode/prefill servers when corresponding Prefill/decode servers go offline
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

I am deploying `qwen3-32b-fp8` in PD disaggregation mode (90 prefill servers + 30 decode servers, all using H20 GPUs). Recently, we encountered a critical cascading failure issue.

When a prefill server is restarted or migrated, the requests currently being processed by the decoder may fail. However, the decode server gets stuck continuously retrying to connect to the downed prefill server. This relentless retrying causes the decode worker's health check to fail or time out with a high probability. Consequently, sglang-router removes these "unhealthy" decoder workers from its available workers list.

While this might seem like a standard non-graceful shutdown issue, it leads to catastrophic consequences in high-QPS scenarios. Once a few prefill servers go offline, a large number of decode servers become unavailable due to health check timeouts. The sglang-router then dispatches all incoming traffic to the few remaining healthy decode servers, which inevitably crash within seconds due to the sudden traffic surge.

I'm currently unsure if the root cause lies within the gateway (e.g., routing to an invalid prefill server URL) or the SGLang server itself (e.g., a dead-loop retry mechanism in the decoder).

Looking for help or any insights on this. Many thanks!

comments.body:
Maybe try `export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=1`?

This can abort all reqs affected in the decode side immediately so that when you restart very quickly, these affected reqs won't trying to reconnect while the new prefill instance is not ready.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
After investigating the scheduler code, we found that the root cause may beyond the `heartbeat_check` failing to evict dead prefill instances from the `prefill_info_table`.

The real bottleneck causing the prolonged blocking is the excessively aggressive 20-retry loop when fetching prefill server info, located here: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/456934fed59eb828e06c116f88c73fc09060d002/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py#L197 and step out here : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/456934fed59eb828e06c116f88c73fc09060d002/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py#L498-L507

It seems the `pending_reqs` list never clears out

Doing 20 synchronous retries is simply too expensive and will quickly starve the asyncio Event Loop, leading to cascading failures like health check timeouts. We definitely need a fast-fail path here to recover normal serving.

In large scale deploment and high-QPS scenarios, I think the time will be much longer. The decoder will definitely be blocking.

As I said above, we need a fast-fail method here. because it lies in the crucial path within the main loop, and `_fetch_prefill_server_info` is synchronously call with `requests.get`, retry with `time.sleep`.

> > [@reporter](https://github.com/reporter) Looks like an NCCL failure (probably because decode node timeout due to the loop in the health check), it should be gone if the decode issue has been fixed.
> 
> [@participant1](https://github.com/participant1) I have to mention again, the decoder instance `10.74.160.156` reported in the log has already been gone for a long time. Means the prefill is keeping connecting to a ghost server, not an "unhealthy" server

@reporter The reason is that the sglang-router still forwards (and retries) the request to the decode instance, even when the prefill node is dead. So the root cause is on the router side. What I am about to do is just to minimize the impact on the decode side when it receives such requests. But I cannot make the router stop sending the requests since we assume this dead prefill is going to be restarted. If you try mini-LB, the issue would not happen, but it is not made for production.

If I kill a decode instance: 

1. `sglang-router` also can't remove the dead decode server in time.
2. `sglang-router` will continuously forward lots of requests to this "dead" decode server paired with all prefill servers. With high-QPS, all prefill instances will **also be blocked by some logic** which I can't find out for now. Leading to prefill-side health_check/chat request failures.

Do you have some insights on this? We also want a fast-fail path if a `prefill` server wants to connect to a "dead" `decode` server.

You're probably right that the root cause lies in `sgl-router`, but right now, we can't find an appropriate solution to remove workers in time. (Doing a health check before every request is not practical)

I ran the test in a 2p2d setup. The reproduction is a bit tricky: since our sglang servers sit behind an `nginx proxy`, I simulate a decode node failure by using `pkill nginx`. This cuts off requests to the sglang port, leaving the decode server unhealthy and unreachable for 60 seconds (our k8s SRE config), then the decode server will be restarted.

@reporter I have tested, the prefill server is not blocked. If you send a request to 2Prefill and another D, they function as normal. The problem here is that you need to send it in 20 seconds, or the detokenizer will timeout, because the current health check logic has a bug, it will mark the prefill server as unhealthy if there are reqs in the queue (any queue) and no results have been forwarded to the detokenizer in 20 seconds. I think this series of problems is all related to the health check part. I will try to fix it when I have some free time.
